title: Does Tech E&O Insurance Cover AI? What Startups Should Check
summary: Does Tech E&O cover AI errors and hallucinations? Learn what to check in exclusions, endorsements and limits, and explore Corgi’s AI coverage options.
body_markdown:
### 1. Does the description match your product?


Explain what your software does, who uses it and what decisions or actions it can make. Include the models and APIs you depend on, whether you fine-tune models, and where a person reviews the output.


If you use another company’s model, review its indemnity separately from your insurance. You still need to understand how your policy treats a claim against your business involving that model.


[Aon’s AI underwriting checklist](https://www.aon.com/risk-services/professional-services/risk-titration-ai-checklist-for-pi-e-and-o) recommends mapping AI uses, oversight, vendor relationships and potential failures. Concrete examples give an underwriter more to work with than “we build AI software.”


### 2. Which AI protection are you buying?


Read the endorsements listed in the proposal alongside the exclusions. Check which activities they address, such as inaccurate outputs, discrimination allegations, training-data disputes or autonomous actions.


The proposal should make clear what is included, what costs extra and what remains excluded. If your product could cause physical injury or damage, raise that explicitly, too.


### 3. How much is available for a claim?


Check these amounts separately:


- Per-claim limit: the most available for one covered claim.


- Aggregate limit: the total available across covered claims during the policy period.


- Any AI sublimit: a smaller limit for a particular AI exposure.


- Retention: the amount your business must pay toward a covered claim.


Also check whether defense costs reduce the limit.


[The Hartford’s Tech E&O renewal information](https://www.thehartford.com/business-insurance-customer-service/tech-error-omission-liability-application-renew) , for example, states that they do under that policy.


A hypothetical quote might show a $1 million overall limit but a $100,000 AI sublimit. For a claim subject to that sublimit, the smaller number matters.


### 4. What about promises in your customer contract?


A customer’s damages claim, a refund and an SLA credit can be treated differently. Bring the insurance clause, performance guarantees and indemnities you’ve agreed to.


For example,


[Corgi’s SLA carveback endorsement](https://www.corgi.insure/tech-eo) can extend protection for certain contractual failures arising from covered wrongful acts. SLA penalties, liquidated damages, service credits and refunds remain excluded.


Check the gap between what your contract promises and what the proposed policy covers before you buy.


### 5. Which dates and reporting rules apply?


For claims-made coverage, check when a claim must first be made against you and when it must be reported. The retroactive date can restrict coverage for earlier work.


If you’re replacing a policy, review continuity before canceling it. Our


[switching guide](https://www.corgi.insure/blog/how-to-switch-business-insurance-providers) explains prior acts, reporting and coverage gaps.
